name: IREN
hq: Sydney, Australia (operations predominantly US: Childress/Sweetwater TX, BC, plus NY and San Francisco hubs)
founded: 2018 by brothers Daniel and Will Roberts (as Iris Energy; renamed IREN Limited November 2024; fiscal year ends June 30)
employees: 257 (Jun 30, 2025) + ~200 site contractors; >3,000 across the Childress build with contractors
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: IREN is the most vertically integrated of the miner-pivots — it owns the land, the substations, the buildings, AND runs the GPU cloud on top — with 5 GW of secured power across three continents, a $9.7B five-year Microsoft GB300 contract whose first liquid-cooled data center (Horizon 1, Childress TX) was delivered and accepted on August 13, 2026, a $3.4B NVIDIA cloud contract plus a 5 GW 'DSX' strategic partnership carrying a $2.1B NVIDIA share-purchase right, and a year-end 2026 ARR target above $4B (~85% contracted). The tension: every quarter of the trailing year missed sell-side consensus (Q3 FY26 revenue missed by 34%), SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX rates the cloud 'Underperforming' even as NVIDIA grants Exemplar Cloud status, and the stock sits ~46% below its November 2025 peak against a Street average target near $80. BACKGROUND: Founded 2018 in Sydney by ex-Macquarie brothers Daniel and Will Roberts as renewable-powered bitcoin miner Iris Energy; peaked at 50 EH/s (June 2025), then began decommissioning miners for GPUs — $172M of ASIC impairments across two quarters, and Bitcoin has vanished from the company boilerplate. FY2025: revenue $501.0M, net income $86.9M. FY2026 annual results land August 27, 2026, with consensus at $722.9M revenue / -$1.57 EPS. Cash ~$7.6B (June 30, preliminary, incl. $1.7B restricted); ~$6.3B of converts outstanding (derived); a $3.65B investment-grade GPU financing (Fitch A) closed June 2026.
ecosystemRole: We assess IREN as the test of whether one company can hold both ends of the AI-infrastructure stack — landlord-grade power ownership (5 GW secured: Childress 750 MW, Sweetwater 2 GW, Oklahoma 1.6 GW, British Columbia 160 MW, Spain 490 MW, Bundey Australia 800 MW) and a climbing cloud business (Mirantis software acquisition, managed services for NVIDIA itself). For power-chain vendors the buildout is unusually visible: IREN owns its ERCOT substations, energized Sweetwater 1's 1.4 GW bulk substation (345/138 kV) on schedule in April 2026, builds 130–200 kW-rack liquid-cooled Horizons at 50 MW IT each, and pairs air-cooled halls (PUE 1.1, BC) with direct-to-chip conversions. Basis: company site-level disclosures and independent trade coverage. The Diligence Stack's taxonomy places IREN between the full-stack platforms ($10–12M revenue/MW) and the pure landlords (~$1.4M/MW) — it is deliberately trying to be both, with newest contracts pricing ~$15M/MW.

productsAndServices.name: IREN Cloud™ (AI Cloud services)
productsAndServices.description: Bare-metal and managed GPU cloud built to NVIDIA reference architecture with non-blocking 3.2 Tb/s InfiniBand: H100/H200, B200 (180GB), B300 (288GB), GB300 NVL72 racks, plus 1.1k AMD MI350X. Fleet trajectory: 1.9k GPUs (Jun 2025) → ~23k (Sep 2025) → purchase agreements taking the fleet toward 150,000 GPUs (Mar 2026). No public rate card — contracts are multi-year (weighted average ~4 years), with recent deals carrying ~45% customer prepayments of associated GPU capex.
highlights: ARR target ladder: >$500M (Sep 2025) → $3.4B → $3.7B → >$4B by YE2026, ~85% contracted (Jul 2026)
Customers: Microsoft, NVIDIA, Perplexity, Figure AI, Together AI, Fluidstack, Fireworks AI, Fal AI, Hume AI
NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on HGX B300 and GB300 NVL72; NVIDIA Preferred Partner
productsAndServices.positioning: The sharpest quality dispute in the cohort: SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX rates IREN 'Underperforming' (vs CoreWeave Platinum, Nebius Gold, Lambda Silver) while NVIDIA's own programs certify it — the Mirantis acquisition (>1,500 enterprise customers, k0rdent AI platform, NVIDIA DSX OS integration) is the answer to the software-maturity gap.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct multi-year contracts; newest deals ~$15M/MW vs the Microsoft anchor at ~$10M/MW (Needham) — pricing power improving as scarcity bites.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 480 MW gross AI-cloud capacity in 2026 → 1.2 GW in 2027; NVIDIA-contract air-cooled Blackwells commissioning early 2027 (ARR to ~$4.4B on commissioning).

productsAndServices.name: AI data centers (own-build, own-power)
productsAndServices.description: End-to-end design/build/operation on owned land with IREN-owned substations. Childress, TX (750 MW, direct ERCOT): Horizon 1–4 — four 50 MW-IT direct-to-chip liquid-cooled buildings for the Microsoft GB300 fleet, Tier 3-equivalent concurrent maintainability, 100 MW superclusters, 130–200 kW racks; Horizon 1 delivered Aug 2026, 2–4 due later in 2026, 5–6 in build for 2027. Sweetwater, TX: 2 GW hub (SW1 1.4 GW — substation energized May 2026; SW2 600 MW, 2027), capable of >700,000 liquid-cooled GPUs, flagged as NVIDIA DSX flagship site. British Columbia: 160 MW air-cooled at PUE 1.1 across Prince George/Mackenzie/Canal Flats, converting from ASICs to GPUs.
highlights: 5 GW secured power, 4,900 acres, 810 MW operational / 2.1 GW under construction / 1.6 GW in development
2028+ pipeline: Oklahoma 1.6 GW (first non-ERCOT), Bundey South Australia 800 MW (four 330 kV feeders), Spain 490 MW via Nostrum
100% renewable via clean grids or REC purchases (the claim Culper contested in 2024)
productsAndServices.positioning: Owns the scarce asset outright — no colocation landlords, no ground leases; Sweetwater has no announced tenant yet, making it the biggest uncontracted power block in the cohort.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Capacity consumed by IREN Cloud contracts today; powered-shell/turnkey colocation offered as the vertical-integration pitch.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 1,210 MW 2027 expansion in build (Horizons 5–6 + Childress air-cooled + Sweetwater 1 initial phase); Oklahoma and Bundey ramp from 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Bitcoin mining (being dismantled)
productsAndServices.description: Peaked at 50 EH/s installed capacity on June 30, 2025 (15 J/TH, ~$41k all-in cash cost per BTC) — 'one of the world's largest and lowest-cost Bitcoin producers.' Since then: ASICs decommissioned ahead of GPU installs ($31.8M + $140.4M impairments in Q2/Q3 FY26), mining revenue -33.6% QoQ by Q3, the Bitcoin vertical dropped from company boilerplate, and no EH/s figure published since October 2025.
highlights: FY2025 mining revenue $484.6M (5,499 BTC) funded the pivot
BC campuses transitioning ASIC→GPU, targeted complete end-2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The fastest, most explicit exit among the big miners — IREN is spending impairments to free megawatts rather than milking the fleet.
productsAndServices.roadmap: No stated end date; the FY26 report (Aug 27) should show how little is left.

productsAndServices.name: Software & platform acquisitions (2026)
productsAndServices.description: Mirantis (closed Aug 4, 2026; ~12.6M shares + ~$40M): cloud software with >1,500 enterprise customers, k0rdent AI orchestration integrated with NVIDIA DSX OS — operates as a standalone subsidiary powering IREN Cloud delivery and the NVIDIA managed-services contract. Nostrum Group (closed Jun 15, 2026): Spanish AI-DC developer with ~490 MW secured grid power and a GW+ pipeline — the Europe entry. Awaken (May 2026): brand/creative agency; founder became CMO.
highlights: Mirantis was the inaugural partner of the NVIDIA AI Cloud Ready Initiative
Three acquisitions in four months — capability shopping at pivot speed
productsAndServices.positioning: Buying the software layer that ClusterMAX says it lacks, rather than building it — the same play as Nebius' Tavily/Eigen buys, a year later.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Mirantis retains standalone enterprise business; the rest folds into IREN's platform.
productsAndServices.roadmap: k0rdent/DSX OS integration is the technical backbone for the NVIDIA managed-cloud ramp (early 2027).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess IREN is executing the most aggressive full-conversion in the cohort — not diversifying from mining but liquidating it. Basis: $172M of voluntary ASIC impairments in two quarters, Bitcoin dropped from the corporate boilerplate and site navigation, monthly mining updates discontinued, and no EH/s figure published since October 2025. The FY26 report (Aug 27) is the last checkpoint where mining still meaningfully colors the numbers.

(High confidence) We assess vertical integration is the genuine differentiator and Sweetwater is its test. Basis: IREN owns land, substations, buildings, and cloud across 5 GW of secured power — landlord economics under cloud revenue ($15M/MW newest contracts vs ~$1.4M/MW pure-landlord colocation). Sweetwater 1's 1.4 GW is energized with no announced tenant; filling it (via the NVIDIA DSX partnership or a hyperscaler) decides whether the integrated model compounds or the power sits as optionality.

(High confidence) We assess the consensus-miss streak is structural, not informational. Basis: every quarter of the trailing year missed (Q3 FY26 by 34% on revenue) because sell-side models can't time mining decommissioning against GPU commissioning; the market has responded by trading contracts and delivery milestones instead — +26% after one miss, -11% after another, depending entirely on what was announced alongside.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the NVIDIA relationship is simultaneously IREN's strongest endorsement and its most cited risk. Basis: NVIDIA is a $3.4B customer, DSX partner, Exemplar Cloud certifier, and holder of a $2.1B share-purchase right — while JPMorgan's Underweight rests precisely on 'the circular nature and undefined access to GPUs' behind the 5 GW ambition. The Aug 27 report and early-2027 NVIDIA-contract commissioning are the verification points.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the quality gap flagged by ClusterMAX ('Underperforming') is real but closing by acquisition. Basis: SemiAnalysis's criteria are software/operations maturity, exactly what Mirantis (>1,500 enterprise customers, NVIDIA DSX OS integration) was bought to fix; Horizon 1's on-time Microsoft acceptance and dual Exemplar Cloud statuses cut against the rating. Collection gap: no independent re-rating since the Mirantis close; the EDNY Culper-era class action's status also remains unresolved in the public record.
